scotch-gambit::0::Nf6@5.say: Nf6 hits e4 before recapturing — answer dxe5. After …Nxe4 the centre clears into a balanced game where your extra space and quicker development give the nagging edge. Develop, seize a file, and squeeze.
scotch-gambit::0::Nf6@5.short: Nf6 — take dxe5, keep the edge.

scotch-gambit::1::Nf6@7.say: Nf6 hits e4 — push e5! and the Max Lange erupts. The pawn cramps, Bb5 looms to pin, and your pieces swarm f7. Black must defend with precision; keep forcing and castle straight into the attack.
scotch-gambit::1::Nf6@7.short: Nf6 — push e5, the Max Lange.

scotch-gambit::0::Ng4@11.say: Ng4 — the knight hops to the rim under your e5-wedge. Brush it back with h3 when ready; for now cxd4 rebuilds the centre and the bishop eyes f7. A pawn down with a commanding initiative.
scotch-gambit::0::Ng4@11.short: Ng4 — cramp with e5, eye f7.

scotch-gambit::0::Ne4@11.say: Ne4 — the knight leaps forward, but it's loose. Hit it with cxd4 and Qe2 or d3, regain the pawn, and your e5-wedge plus the bishop on f7 keep Black scrambling. Develop with threats.
scotch-gambit::0::Ne4@11.short: Ne4 — chase it, keep the wedge.

scotch-gambit::0::Qe7@11.say: Qe7 leans on your e5-pawn — defend it dynamically. cxd4 and O-O finish development, Re1 backs the wedge, and the bishop glares at f7. Black's queen is awkward there; press the initiative.
scotch-gambit::0::Qe7@11.short: Qe7 — back e5, develop and press.

scotch-gambit::0::Ng8@11.say: Ng8 — the knight crawls all the way home! You've won the centre and a fistful of tempi. cxd4, Bf4 and the rooks pour out while Black is curled up on the back rank. A pawn down and utterly dominating.
scotch-gambit::0::Ng8@11.short: Ng8 — it retreated; pour it on.

scotch-gambit::0::Nd7@13.say: Nd7 unpins the c6-knight, but your bishop on b5 still bites and the e5-wedge cramps. cxd4 rebuilds the centre, O-O and Re1 follow, and your space and development are well worth the pawn.

scotch-gambit::0::Bg4@17.say: Bg4 pins your f3-knight deep in the Max Lange — meet it with Be2 or h3 and keep building. Your e5-pawn and d4-centre cramp, the pieces are active, and the sharp position favours the better-prepared attacker. Stay precise.
scotch-gambit::0::Bg4@17.short: Bg4 — break the pin, keep building.

scotch-gambit::0::Ng4@13.say: Ng4 hops to the rim under your e5-wedge. Brush it back with h3 when it suits; cxd4 rebuilds, Bb5 pins, and your space plus the open lines keep the initiative. The gambit pawn buys real pressure.

scotch-gambit::0::Qe7@13.say: Qe7 props the position under the e5-wedge — but the queen sits passive there. cxd4 and O-O finish development, the b5-bishop pins, and you press the cramped, awkward black camp. The pawn is a small price.

scotch-gambit::1::Bc5@7.say: Bc5 — the main Scotch Gambit. Strike with c3 to recover d4, or e5 and the Max Lange. Your bishop is on f7, development races, and the pawn buys a roaring initiative. Castle and attack.
scotch-gambit::1::Bc5@7.short: Bc5 — c3 or e5, attack f7.

scotch-gambit::2::Bc5@7.say: Bc5 — the main Scotch Gambit. Strike with c3 to recover d4, or e5 and the Max Lange. Your bishop is on f7, development races, and the pawn buys a roaring initiative. Castle and attack.
scotch-gambit::2::Bc5@7.short: Bc5 — c3 or e5, attack f7.

evans-gambit::0::Be7@5.say: Be7 — Black sidesteps into a passive Hungarian. Take the space: d4 builds the full centre, or b4 grabs the Evans initiative anyway. Castle, develop freely, and squeeze the cramped, counterplay-free position.
evans-gambit::0::Be7@5.short: Be7 — take the centre with d4.

evans-gambit::0::Be7@9.say: Be7 — the meek retreat in the accepted Evans. Build the dream: d4 plants the centre, Ba3 rakes the bishop on e7 and the king, and you've a roaring initiative for the pawn. Develop and attack.

evans-gambit::0::Bb6@7.say: Bb6 declines the pawn for the quieter Evans. Make the tempo tell: a4 lunges at the queenside, threatening a5 to chase or trap the bishop. Then Nc3, d3 and a calm build-up leave you more space and the easier game.
evans-gambit::0::Bb6@7.short: Bb6 — harass with a4, gain space.

evans-gambit::2::d6@11.say: d6 props the centre in the quiet Evans. Hold your edge: a4 and a5 have prised the queenside, Nc3 and d3 develop, and you prepare d4 or the f-file. More space, the easier game — squeeze.

evans-gambit::2::a5@9.say: a5 halts your a-pawn but bites on b5 and c5 — squares your knight covets. Nc3, d3 and a slow build leave you the freer game; the b5-outpost and your central space are the lasting assets.
evans-gambit::2::a5@9.short: a5 — use the b5 hole, build.

evans-gambit::2::h6@13.say: h6 — a useful luft in the quiet Evans, nothing forcing. Continue the plan: O-O, then prepare d4 or Bg5 and the f-file. Your queenside space and the better bishop give a small, lasting pull — out-manoeuvre him.

evans-gambit::2::O-O@13.say: O-O — Black castles into the quiet Evans. Now turn the screw: d4 challenges the centre, or Bg5 pins and the rooks swing over. Your queenside space from a4-a5 and the active bishops give the pull — press it.
evans-gambit::2::O-O@13.short: O-O — challenge d4, swing the rooks.

evans-gambit::2::Nxb4@13.say: Nxb4 grabs the b-pawn — but it loosens Black's grip and the knight strays. Hit back with d4, opening the centre while the b4-knight is offside; your bishops and the open lines more than answer the pawn.
evans-gambit::2::Nxb4@13.short: Nxb4 — open d4, the knight strays.

evans-gambit::2::Nd4@13.say: Nd4 jumps to the centre — challenge it: Nxd4 Bxd4 hands you the bishop pair and the freer game, or sidestep and keep the tension. Your queenside space and active pieces hold the edge.
evans-gambit::2::Nd4@13.short: Nd4 — challenge Nxd4, take the pair.

evans-gambit::2::Ng4@13.say: Ng4 lunges at f2 — calmly parried. With your king's bishop covering and pieces developed, brush it back with h3 and Black is loosened with nothing to show. Continue d4 and the squeeze.
evans-gambit::2::Ng4@13.short: Ng4 — brush it back with h3.

evans-gambit::1::Bd6@9.say: Bd6 — the solid modern retreat, overprotecting e5 and blocking Black's own d-pawn. Roll on: d4 and O-O keep the broad centre and the bishop pair, and patient pressure on the cramped position is the way, the pawn a fair price.
evans-gambit::1::Bd6@9.short: Bd6 — d4 and O-O, press the cramp.

evans-gambit::3::Nf6@11.say: Nf6 develops against your big centre — keep building. O-O, then the d4-e5 push or Bg5 pile pressure on. Your centre and the bishop pair are the engine; turn the initiative the pawn bought into an attack.

evans-gambit::3::Nf6@13.say: Nf6 finally develops, but you're already castled and active. Re1 backs the centre, e5 or Bg5 strike, and the bishops rake Black's cramped camp. Convert the lead in development the gambit bought.

evans-gambit::3::exd4@13.say: exd4 finally grabs the centre pawn — recapture cxd4 and your broad duo stands, the bishops blaze, the rooks own the open lines. A pawn down and dominating; pour the pieces at the king.

evans-gambit::3::Qf6@13.say: Qf6 eyes f2 and develops — but the queen blocks Black's own pieces. Hold firm with Be3 or Nbd2, keep the centre, and your faster development and bishop pair tell. Develop with threats.

evans-gambit::3::Qe7@13.say: Qe7 props the cramped position passively. Press your trumps: the d4-centre, the bishops, the open lines. Nbd2-f1-g3 or e5 turns the screw, and the initiative is full value for the pawn.
evans-gambit::3::Qe7@13.short: Qe7 — press the centre and bishops.
